nextStoryContext: US-R1-004 fixed README.md staleness flagged by the round-1 review: the CAM-42 'Interactive TUI workers' invariant bullet (README.md:419, Recent changes) and the parallel absolute claim in the Architecture section (README.md:382, 'claude -p (print mode) is not used for workers') both predated the CAM-516/ADR-0059 recorte (the claude -p prohibition is recortada, not aposentada; `cam next --headless` is a pure per-invocation, never-persisted, never-sticky flag that opts the implementer worker into a claude -p/stream-json dispatch, exempted by a 2026-08-08 measurement showing unchanged console API consumption and a subscription-window rate_limit_event, not a per-use charge). Fixed both bullets to state the default-is-TUI / headless-is-opt-in shape instead of an absolute 'claude -p never used' claim, added `--headless` to the `cam next [options]` line in the Commands list (was literally 'cam next [options]', now 'cam next [--headless]'), and added a short options note (mirroring the existing permission-mode note directly below the command list) documenting what `--headless` does and cross-referencing ADR-0059. Doc-only change: no source files touched, no external library involved (Step 5.5: lib=none). Scope stayed surgical to the staleness class the WARNING named (the claude -p / interactive-TUI narrative) -- did NOT touch the unrelated `cam`-vs-`gship` binary-name terminology used throughout the same README (package.json's bin is now {gateship, gship}, no `cam` binary name), since that is a separate, much larger naming-migration concern out of scope for this doc-sync story. Next implementer picking up a US-R1-* story from this round-1 review batch: prd.json still carries US-R1-005 (headless ignoring implBackend in loop.ts's dispatch branch, touched by US-R1-002/003) and a sixth round-1 finding, both passes:false -- see openQuestions.
